rounds.text: Revathi Equipment India Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a margin of safety calculated at 70.8% [E37]. The market is failing to price in the company's operational momentum, as evidenced by a P/E ratio of 11.2x compared to the sector benchmark of 21.44x [E1, E6]. This undervaluation is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 8.1x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 12.02x [E11]. Recent performance shows a dramatic turnaround, with quarterly operating margins expanding by 17 percentage points year-over-year [E22] and net profit growth reaching 762% [E59]. While the stock has suffered from negative sentiment, the company is actively strengthening its balance sheet by reducing borrowings from Rs 68 Cr to Rs 54 Cr [E30]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow [E25, E26], high debtor days [E53], and a lack of dividend payouts [E4, E51].

Revathi Equipment India Ltd presents significant operational risks, most notably evidenced by a catastrophic cash conversion ratio of -2.07x and negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -29 Cr and Rs -43 Cr respectively [E25, E26, E27]. This inability to generate cash from operations is compounded by deteriorating working capital efficiency, as working capital days have nearly doubled from 43.7 to 80.1 days [E55]. Furthermore, the company suffers from high debtor days of 156, suggesting a structural difficulty in collecting payments that threatens liquidity [E53]. The stock’s technical profile remains deeply concerning, with a -27.8% twelve-month return, a position below both the 50-day and 200-day moving averages, and a history of extreme volatility reaching an 85.5% peak-to-trough drawdown [E41, E43, E44, E45]. While the company reports profits, the absence of any dividend payout and the reliance on Rs 9.93 Cr of other income to bolster earnings raise questions about the quality of these results [E4, E51, E52]. Conceded: the company shows strong recent profit growth of 78% and trades at a P/E of 11.2x, which is below the sector benchmark [E1, E17, E6].

The bear’s focus on cash flow ignores the company’s aggressive deleveraging, as borrowings have been reduced to Rs 54 Cr from Rs 68 Cr in the prior year [E30]. While the bear highlights negative cash flow, it overlooks the massive operational turnaround evidenced by the quarterly operating margin jumping 17 percentage points to 13% in Sep 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E22]. Conceded: the company reported negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -29 Cr and Rs -43 Cr in Mar 2026 [E26, E27]. However, the bear’s reliance on stale technicals ignores that profit growth is currently outpacing one-year price growth by 101%, signaling that the market is beginning to misprice the company's improving fundamentals [E48]. Furthermore, the bear’s critique of "other income" ignores the broader reality that the company is currently flagged for an expected good quarter [E50]. Finally, while the bear cites high debtor days, it fails to acknowledge that the company is operating within a sector currently experiencing a tailwind, which provides a supportive macro backdrop for resolving these working capital inefficiencies [E53, E62].

Conceded: borrowings have decreased to Rs 54 Cr from Rs 68 Cr [E30], and quarterly operating margin rose to 13% in Sep 2026 [E22]. However, pointing to deleveraging does not erase the severe cash burn of Rs -29 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs -43 Cr in free cash flow reported in Mar 2026 [E26, E27]. The bull's dismissal of these cash figures is perilous when paired with ballooning working capital days, which surged from 43.7 to 80.1 days alongside high debtors of 156 days [E53, E55]. Furthermore, leaning on an expected good quarter [E50] ignores the reality that reported earnings are contaminated by Rs 9.93 Cr of other income rather than pure operational strength [E52]. Conceded: profit growth is outpacing one-year price growth [E48], but this momentum is undermined by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E23, E24] and a dismal relative-strength rating of 38 [E42]. Finally, citing a sector tailwind [E62] does nothing to insulate the company from its own internal structural weaknesses, including a 0.00% dividend yield [E4] and returns on equity that languish below sector benchmarks at 8.6% [E9, E13].
